kept.title: Zip Slip Vulnerability in extraction
kept.description: The library does not sufficiently sanitize file paths when extracting files, potentially allowing an attacker to overwrite arbitrary files on the system outside the target directory (Zip Slip).
steps_to_exploit: Craft a malicious ZIP archive where a filename contains '../' sequences.
Extract the archive using adm-zip's extraction methods.
The library's path resolution does not block traversal to unintended locations.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution or file system corruption via arbitrary file write.

kept.title: Use of Weak/Broken ZipCrypto
kept.description: The library uses legacy ZipCrypto which is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to plaintext attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Capture an encrypted file from a ZIP archive.
Obtain even a small amount of plaintext data for a file in the archive.
Use public tools like 'bkcrack' to recover the internal keys and decrypt the files.
kept.impact: Complete loss of confidentiality for protected files.

kept.title: Integer Overflow in ZIP64 offset calculation
kept.description: The logic to handle ZIP64 offsets and sizes is prone to overflow issues when converting 64-bit values to JS Numbers if inputs are maliciously crafted.
steps_to_exploit: Create a ZIP archive with a specifically crafted ZIP64 header.
Set field values to numbers that cause truncation or precision loss during parsing.
Trigger unexpected behavior in the central directory indexing.
kept.impact: Denial of service or incorrect file access via corrupted indexing.

kept.title: Insecure permissions set on extracted files
kept.description: Files extracted from the ZIP are written with default permissions that may be overly permissive or inherited incorrectly.
steps_to_exploit: Extract a file from an archive containing sensitive data.
The library applies 0o666 or inconsistent chmod logic.
The file is readable/writable by unauthorized local users.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to sensitive extracted data on shared file systems.

kept.title: Potential prototype pollution via Object.assign
kept.description: The library uses Object.assign on user-provided inputs to initialize configuration, which could lead to prototype pollution.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a malicious JSON object containing '__proto__' or 'constructor' properties to the constructor.
The library merges these into the configuration object.
This affects subsequent logic reliant on these configuration properties.
kept.impact: Global application instability or altered logic flow.

kept.title: Directory Traversal in addLocalFile
kept.description: The `addLocalFile` function does not fully sanitize the `zipPath` argument, allowing files to be placed in unexpected relative paths within the archive.
steps_to_exploit: Invoke `addLocalFile` with a `zipPath` containing '../../'.
The library adds the file to an arbitrary location in the zip structure.
This can lead to overwriting files if the zip is later extracted improperly.

kept.title: Denial of Service via decompression loop
kept.description: There is no limit on the size of uncompressed data relative to the compressed input, allowing 'zip bombs' to exhaust memory.
steps_to_exploit: Create a highly compressed ZIP file (zip bomb).
Call an extraction method on the file.
The `inflate` logic will attempt to allocate memory for the full size, crashing the process.
kept.impact: Denial of Service via resource exhaustion.

kept.title: Unsafe random number generator for salt
kept.description: The `genSalt.node` fallback uses `Math.random()`, which is not cryptographically secure.
steps_to_exploit: Force the system to use the `genSalt.node` fallback (if `crypto` is not available or mocked).
Predict salt generation for encrypted archives.
Lower the effort required for password cracking attacks.
kept.impact: Weakened security for encrypted ZIP files.

kept.title: Lack of input validation on header length fields
kept.description: The library reads length fields from the ZIP header and uses them for buffer slicing without verifying if they exceed the remaining buffer size.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a ZIP file where a `fileNameLength` or `extraFieldLength` is extremely large.
The code slices past the end of the buffer or throws an unhandled error.
This can crash the event loop.

kept.title: Insecure use of `console.warn` for critical error
kept.description: Path validation failures are logged to the console but the execution continues, potentially using invalid or empty states.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger the invalid path branch in `fattr.js`.
The object is returned in a partially initialized, invalid state.
Subsequent logic performs operations on this uninitialized object.
kept.impact: Unexpected application state leading to potential bugs.

kept.title: Weak validation of ZIP signature
kept.description: The library performs a 'quick check' for the character 'P' before validating the signature, which might be bypassed by malicious files.
steps_to_exploit: Create a file with a fake signature that starts with 'P' but is not a valid ZIP.
The library may attempt to parse it incorrectly.
This leads to incorrect processing of malicious files.
kept.impact: Potential logic bypass or crashes during parsing.

evidence.quote: if (inBuffer[i] !== 0x50) continue; // quick check that the byte is 'P'

kept.title: Insufficient error handling in async chains
kept.description: Errors in recursive async callbacks are not always propagated correctly, potentially leaving the application in a hung state.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an I/O error mid-way through `addLocalFolderAsync2`.
The reduction chain fails to clean up or pass the error to the final callback.
The process may stop without notifying the user.

kept.title: Potential for filename injection via non-normalized input
kept.description: Filename inputs passed to `addFile` are not checked for dangerous characters that might interfere with file system operations (e.g., control characters).
steps_to_exploit: Inject a filename with null bytes or shell metacharacters.
The file is created with an unexpected name.
This can be used to trick other system tools that read the archive.
kept.impact: File system confusion and potential secondary vulnerability in tools parsing these archives.

kept.title: Global configuration vulnerability in ZipCrypto
kept.description: The `_salter` function allows a user to redefine the global `genSalt` function, which affects all instances of the library.
steps_to_exploit: Call `_salter` to modify the global salt generation.
Subsequent encryption in other parts of the application uses the weakened salt.
This effectively disables randomization for all users.
kept.impact: Total loss of entropy in encryption across the process.

kept.title: Excessive reliance on synchronous I/O in constructors
kept.description: The library reads entire files into memory synchronously during initialization, which can block the event loop and lead to DoS.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a large file path to the library constructor.
The library calls `readFileSync`.
The main event loop becomes unresponsive until the entire file is loaded.
kept.impact: Event loop block, leading to Denial of Service in server environments.
